note: PASS WITH ONE REAL CAVEAT (item order within the subscale is inferred). (1) SOURCE: the study deposits both halves. The S1 Appendix prints the administered Spanish beside the study's own English for all 45 retained items; the S1 Dataset .sav carries the English response anchors as value labels (1 'Totally disagree', 2 'Disagree', 3 'Partially disagree', 4 'Not in disagree or agree', 5 'Partially agree', 6 'Agree', 7 'Totally agree'), identical for all seven items. Spanish ships in the base fields, English in item_text_translated / option_text_translated, language=Spanish. (2) MAPPING, derivation pattern 1: data/avilatamayo_2022_csr.py selects columns by the prefix 'Work_Life' and calls df.melt(value_vars=item_cols, var_name='item') with no rename, so the IRW code IS the .sav column name -- no positional step. But mapping_basis is paper_order, NOT data_labels: the .sav variable labels are bare ordinals ('Work-life balance 4'), so the words come from the appendix, whose rows are numbered by nothing. THE NUMBERING GAP: the live codes are 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8 -- position 3 is absent from the deposit entirely, and the paper states 'three items were dropped due to small loadings ... one from skill development, one from work-life balance, and one from tangible employee involvement'. The appendix reproduces the RETAINED items only, so its seven work-life rows were read against the .sav column ORDER (rows 1-7 -> 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8) rather than counted off 1..7; the dropped item's wording is published nowhere and is NOT in this file. Corroborating structure, not proof: the appendix's seven block sizes are 7/5/6/6/7/6/8 and the .sav's per-prefix column counts are 7/5/6/6/7/6/8, matching one for one, and each block's final row is its 'En general / Overall' summary item, which lands on the block's highest code (Work_Life_5.8_1). (3) STEP 5b -- PARTIAL, see verify_avilatamayo_2022_work_life.R. Route 9 is decisive on the option axis: all 49 item x level cell counts computed from the raw .sav match the live table exactly (e.g. 5.2_1: 55/27/40/55/91/96/69; 5.8_1: 30/37/54/95/81/92/44), so the 1..7 integers are the source's own codes unrecoded and the anchors attach in the source's order. Route 3 pins membership and rules out reverse-scoring: the seven live items composite to M=4.1819, SD=1.4078 (n=432 complete) against the paper's Table 1 Work-life balance 4.19 / 1.41 -- deviations 0.0081 and 0.0022. Route 8 is consistent: the two concrete commitments are the two least endorsed (5.1 child-care programmes 3.635; 5.5 policies forbidding forced overtime 3.861) while the generic coordination item 5.4 carries the block's highest corrected item-total r (0.792 against 0.530-0.753), the ordering item content predicts. ONE PUBLISHED STATISTIC DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and it is recorded rather than explained away: Cronbach's alpha is 0.8835 observed against a published .90. It is not a scoring-direction artefact (M and SD reproduce to 0.008 and 0.002, and every reversal tried moves M by ~1.6). Recomputing all seven ICSR subscales from the .sav reproduces five published alphas to two decimals (.9196/.92, .8772/.87, .9254/.93, .8971/.89) and misses two -- work-life balance (.8835 vs .90) and tangible employee involvement (.9380 vs .95). The likeliest reading is that those two alphas were computed before the item drop, on a set this deposit does not contain; it cannot be checked, because the dropped columns are not in the .sav. This does not bear on which text goes with which code. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the order of the seven texts within the subscale. The paper publishes no per-item statistic at all -- Table 1 is construct-level, Fig 2 is a second-order path diagram carrying seven construct loadings, and the text reports only a mean loading per factor ('work-life balance = 0.71'). Items 5.6 and 5.8 have means 4.4527 and 4.4134, so a swap of those two would be undetectable. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. (4) STEP 3b: the table is the right block. Live items are the seven Work_Life codes, resp 1-7, n=432-433 each, matching the appendix's seven-row 'Equilibrio entre vida laboral y vida familiar' block and the dictionary's 'work-life balance subscale, N=433'. The paper's other six ICSR dimensions and the Meyer/Allen commitment scale are separate columns and separate IRW tables. Seven distinct items, so the no-single-item bar is cleared. (5) TRANSCRIPTION: verbatim, with the deviations named. Leading/trailing whitespace was stripped from the appendix cells. The instructions paragraph ships exactly as printed, including its unclosed parenthesis ('...7 = totalmente de acuerdo.') and its lowercase anchors; the Spanish option_text is those anchors as the instruction line spells them, not recapitalised. The appendix's en-dash spacing in 'balance vida - trabajo' is left as printed. (6) instructions_translated is NOT emitted: the appendix prints the administration instructions in Spanish only, and translating them here would put IRW-generated English in a content field. All English that ships is the study's own, hence translation_source=study_supplied and nothing was machine-translated. section_prompt is blank and section_id is the single trivial avilatamayo_2022_work_life_1 -- the appendix's 'Equilibrio entre vida laboral y vida familiar' heading is a dimension label, not a prompt, and is recorded in `instrument`. correct_response blank (attitude scale). (7) DATA NOTE, not a text defect: Work_Life_5.4_1 holds one non-integer cell (3.8308457711442787), the paper's stated mean-imputation for its <2% missing data; the processing script drops it, which is why that item carries n=432 against 433 for the other six. (8) RIGHTS: no block, and no reserved right locatable. The Spanish wording is the study's own translation, published in its CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE appendix. The upstream instrument is Mory et al.'s ICSR Q, an academic scale carried in a journal article and not sold by a test publisher; a search for a licence, fee, permission-required or non-commercial statement for the ICSR Q found none to quote. instrument_rights_register.csv holds no row for this instrument or family (grepped for 'ICSR', 'Mory', 'corporate social'). Silence is permission, so extracted normally; no register row written (a round may write `block`, never `ship`). (9) SIBLINGS: empl_stab, skills_dev and work_envir shipped in batch_274 from this same .sav and appendix, and workf_div is being handled elsewhere in this round. Nothing was written for any of them here. The batch_274 convention is reused unchanged (Spanish base fields, study's English in _translated, blank instructions_translated, single trivial section_id, paper_order + PARTIAL), which is corroboration rather than a new decision. (10) RETRY TEST: NO. The CSV is written and the gate passed; an unchanged retry would produce the identical file. The two open items are determinate gaps, not access failures: the within-subscale order cannot be upgraded because the paper publishes no per-item statistic and the appendix numbers no row, and the alpha gap cannot be resolved because the dropped column is not in the deposit. Only new material from the authors, or Mory et al.'s original item numbering, would change either.
public_note: The Spanish item wording, the response anchors and the instructions are transcribed verbatim from the study's own CC BY appendix and data file, and the English alongside is the study's own rendering, not an IRW translation. Two things are worth knowing. First, this subscale lost one item before publication: the live codes run Work_Life_5.1_1, 5.2_1, then 5.4_1 through 5.8_1, with no 5.3, and the dropped item's wording is published nowhere. The appendix numbers none of its rows, so the assignment of its seven sentences to those codes follows the appendix's presentation order together with the data file's own ordinal labels ('Work-life balance 1', '... 2', '... 4' .. '... 8'); with no per-item statistics published anywhere in the paper, that order could not be checked item by item, and items 5.6 and 5.8 have means 4.45 and 4.41, so a swap between them would be undetectable. What was checked against the data: all 49 item-by-response-level counts in the raw SPSS file match the live table exactly, so the 1-7 anchors attach in the source's own order, and the seven items composite to M=4.18, SD=1.41 against the paper's published 4.19 / 1.41, so the subscale membership is right and the items are stored raw rather than reverse-scored. Second, the paper's published Cronbach's alpha of .90 for this subscale does not reproduce from the deposited data, which gives .88; the same gap appears in the tangible-employee-involvement subscale, and both are subscales that lost an item, so the published figures were most likely computed before the drop. The instructions ship in Spanish only; the appendix prints no English version of them.

note: Item codes ARE the S1 Dataset (s002.csv) column headers -- data/busch_2022_course_depression.py melts the 17 idep.* columns with no renaming -- and each header names its own aspect (idep.proctor.exam, idep.home.distract), so code->aspect needs no positional inference. item_text is the literal option list of Q104 in the S1 Appendix survey copy ('Please select all aspects of ONLINE college science courses that might make your feelings of depression worse'), transcribed verbatim including the '(e.g., during exams)' / '(e.g., unstable internet connection)' parentheticals; idep.other ships the survey's 'Other, please describe' (the trailing write-in blank is dropped). instructions concatenate the survey's own framing line, the Q152 depression-block preamble and the Q104 stem, verbatim. The header->wording tie was additionally checked against data rather than asserted: S1 Appendix Table S5 publishes a separate demographic linear-probability model per aspect LABELLED BY ITS FULL WORDING, and refitting that model on each idep.* column reproduces all 17 published coefficient vectors to <=0.005 (the 2 d.p. rounding floor) with a unique nearest match each time -- see verify_busch_2022_course_exacerbate.R. Aspect order in Table S5 is also the alphabetical order of the idep.* column suffixes, with 'nothing' and 'other' last. Rights: the wording is the study's own author-written checklist, not a published instrument, in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article; no rights holder clause locatable and none applies. Same shape and same lab as the cooper_2018_funny_topics/_offensive_topics precedent (batch_023).
public_note: This battery is a select-all-that-apply checklist, so `resp` is a checkbox state rather than a chosen response option, and the `option_text` values 'Selected' and 'Not selected' describe that 0/1 coding rather than transcribing anything the survey printed -- the source publishes no response labels for it, only the stem 'Please select all aspects of ONLINE college science courses that might make your feelings of depression worse.'
